patients.summary: Restoration contractor and heavy smoker who joined in 2023, was found to have poorly controlled type 2 diabetes in 2024, then had pulmonary histoplasmosis from bat-dropping attic work, a left leg cellulitis, and a pneumonia admission he left against advice. Basal insulin was added in 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43 y/o man new to the practice. Hasn't had a regular doctor in several years, last physical he can remember was for a job. Wants a doctor he can actually reach. No complaints today.

Work: runs a small building restoration business, a lot of old houses and barns, crawl spaces, attics. Wears a dust mask 'when it's really bad.'
Tobacco: about a pack a day since he was 15, so roughly 30 pack-years. Has tried cutting down, never a formal quit attempt.
Alcohol: a beer or two on weekends.
PMH: nothing chronic. PSH: tonsils out at 12.
Meds: none. Allergies: none known.
Family: father has type 2 diabetes, found around 50. Mother has high blood pressure. An uncle on his father's side had lung cancer.

ROS: negative across the board. No cough.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT unremarkable, tonsillar pillars surgically absent. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid not enlarged. Lungs clear, good air movement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Legs without edema. Skin no lesions of concern.

Assessment/plan:
1. Tobacco dependence. Spent a few minutes on this. Not ready for a quit date. Offered nicotine replacement or varenicline, he'd rather not right now. Will keep asking.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, hep C screen today. Tdap given (can't recall last tetanus, works with nails and old lumber all day). Flu and COVID in the fall.
3. Family hx of diabetes noted; will look at labs.

RTC for a physical next spring, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated well, waited 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi David, your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and hepatitis C screen all came back fine. Nothing to act on. Good to meet you. The offer on quitting help stands whenever you want it.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines

documents.body: Came in after work for vaccines. No fever or illness today. Flu 0.5 mL IM L arm, COVID (2023-24 formula) IM R arm. Observed 15 minutes, fine. Reminded about physical in the spring.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44M here for his yearly exam. Says that for the last few weeks he's been thirsty all the time and up twice a night to urinate, figured it was the heat on job sites. Down a couple of pounds without trying. No vision change. No foot numbness.

Still smoking about a pack a day. Alcohol unchanged.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Chest clear. Heart regular without murmur. Abdomen soft. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, DP and PT pulses 2+ both sides. No edema.

Labs drawn this morning: glucose 210, A1c 9.6, both back this afternoon. Called him.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes, new, A1c 9.6. Long talk by phone after the result. Father's history fits. Starting metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals, will step up in a few weeks if GI tolerates. Diet basics, cutting the sweet tea and soda he drinks on site. Referral info for diabetes education class given. Will get urine albumin and lipids at follow-up. Eye exam to be set up.
2. Tobacco: brought up again now with diabetes in the picture. Not ready. Declines medication.
3. Pneumococcal vaccine indicated (diabetes, smoker); he'll stop in tomorrow for it.

Follow-up portal check in a month, visit in about 4 months.

documents.title: Immunization

documents.body: Came by on lunch break. PCV20 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Tolerated well.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

documents.title: Message from patient
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc, the metformin is fine. Stomach was off the first week, ok now. Not as thirsty. Haven't made the class yet, work is crazy.

documents.title: Re: metformin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it settled. Let's move up to the full dose: one 1000 mg tablet twice a day with food. New prescription sent, finish or toss the 500s. If your stomach acts up again, let me know. See you in September with labs.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily before breakfast

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: On metformin 1000 BID since June, taking it most days, misses the evening dose when he eats late on the road. Thirst gone. Never made the education class. Diet 'better than it was.' Smoking the same.

O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear. RRR. Feet intact, sensation normal to monofilament, pulses good.
A1c 8.8 (from 9.6). LDL 118. Urine albumin/creatinine normal. Kidney function fine.

A/P:
1. T2DM, improved but well above goal. Adding glipizide 10 mg each morning before breakfast. Went over low sugar symptoms and treatment, he works on ladders so eat breakfast if he takes it. Glucometer script sent; check fasting a few mornings a week.
2. Lipids reviewed.
3. Eye exam: gave him the optometry list again.
4. Tobacco: 1 minute, same answer.

Flu and COVID next month. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Eye Examination Report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Outside optometry office. Exam date 2024-11-12.
Patient: David Thayer, DOB 12/02/1979. Reason: annual diabetic eye exam, type 2 diabetes since spring 2024.
Meds per patient: metformin, glipizide. Allergies: NKDA.
Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS uncorrected. Pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect. IOP 15/16. Dilated fundus exam: clear media, discs sharp and pink, vessels normal caliber, maculae flat. No hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization in either eye.
Impression: no diabetic retinopathy.
Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.
Thank you for the referral.

events.reason: Cough for nearly 3 months, weight loss

reports.text:
Clinical history: cough for about 11 weeks, weight loss, night sweats, current smoker.
Technique: PA and lateral views of the chest.
Comparison: none available.
Findings: Multiple small nodular opacities are scattered throughout both lungs. Both hila are enlarged and lobulated, consistent with hilar lymphadenopathy. No lobar consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Bones and soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Multiple small bilateral pulmonary nodular opacities with hilar lymphadenopathy. Infectious or granulomatous process favored in the clinical setting; other causes not excluded. Recommend clinical correlation and specialist evaluation.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: bilateral nodular opacities, hilar adenopathy, weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit - Cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: cough since mid-November.

HPI: Dry cough that hasn't let up in about 11 weeks. Thought it was a cold, then 'smoker's cough,' but it's been getting him up at night. More tired than he's ever been, cutting jobs short by early afternoon. Clothes looser, and the scale here is about 5 kg under his spring weight without any dieting. Some nights he wakes damp, not drenching. Feels feverish on and off, low grade when he's checked, around 100.
No blood in sputum. No chest pain. Some breathlessness on ladders that's new.
Exposure: asked about work. In October he spent a few weeks gutting and cleaning out attics in a couple of old vacant buildings, several of them thick with bat droppings. Mask on 'most of the time.'
Still smoking a pack a day. Sugars at home in the 170-190 range fasting. Taking metformin and glipizide.

Exam: tired looking, a bit pale. Vitals as charted. No nodes in neck or supraclavicular area. Lungs: scattered fine crackles both sides, no wheeze. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen felt. No clubbing, no edema.

CXR done downstairs this afternoon, I looked at it with him: lots of small nodules both lungs and big hila. Formal read agrees.

A/P:
1. Subacute cough, weight loss, sweats, bilateral nodular opacities with hilar adenopathy after heavy bat-dropping exposure. Endemic fungal infection is high on the list; malignancy and other granulomatous disease need to be excluded in a 30 pack-year smoker. Urgent pulmonology referral placed, called their office, he's on for 2/12. CBC, BMP today.
2. T2DM, A1c 8.9. Not the day to change things, he has enough going on. Continue metformin 1000 BID and glipizide 10.
3. Tobacco: he says this scared him a little. Still not setting a date.

Call with fevers above 101, coughing blood, or worse breathing.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE CONSULTATION (outside group)
Date of service: 02/12/2025
Re: David Thayer, DOB 12/02/1979
Referring: primary care physician

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Thayer, a 45-year-old restoration contractor, for three months of a nonproductive cough with lung nodules and hilar adenopathy.

History: the cough started around mid-November and has been steady. Over the same stretch he has become progressively fatigued and lost weight without trying, with low-grade fevers off and on and mild sweats at night. About four months ago he spent a period cleaning out several attics in old abandoned structures that were heavily soiled with bat guano.
PMH: type 2 diabetes, poorly controlled, diagnosed last spring. Tobacco use disorder.
PSH: tonsillectomy as a child.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; glipizide 10 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: current smoker, 30 pack-years. Alcohol 1-2 drinks weekly.
Family: father with type 2 diabetes; mother with hypertension; paternal uncle with lung cancer.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Mild pallor of the conjunctivae and skin. No lymphadenopathy palpable in the neck. Scattered crackles are heard over both lung fields; no wheezes. Cardiac exam regular without murmur. No hepatosplenomegaly. No clubbing.

Data: chest radiograph from 01/28/2025 reviewed personally, showing multiple small nodular opacities throughout both lungs together with hilar lymphadenopathy. HIV screen sent today: nonreactive.

Impression: subacute illness with diffuse small nodules and hilar nodes after a heavy bat-guano exposure. Pulmonary histoplasmosis is the leading concern. Tissue is needed to confirm and to exclude malignancy given his smoking.

Plan: flexible bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsies, scheduled 02/19. We will be in touch with results and treatment. Smoking cessation strongly advised.

Pulmonology

reports.text:
Specimen: lung, transbronchial biopsies, multiple fragments.
Gross: received in formalin, five tan-pink tissue fragments, the largest 0.3 cm, entirely submitted.
Microscopic: alveolated lung tissue with collections of histiocytes. Silver and PAS stains highlight numerous small, uniform ovoid yeast forms within macrophages, measuring about 2 to 4 microns. No malignancy identified.
reports.conclusion: Lung, transbronchial biopsy: intracellular small ovoid yeast forms within macrophages, consistent with histoplasmosis. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy Report
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
BRONCHOSCOPY PROCEDURE NOTE
Date: 02/19/2025
Indication: bilateral pulmonary nodular opacities and hilar lymphadenopathy, suspected endemic fungal infection.
Consent: risks including bleeding, pneumothorax and infection discussed; consent signed.
Sedation: moderate sedation with continuous monitoring.
Procedure: flexible bronchoscope passed through the mouth. Vocal cords normal. Airways inspected to the subsegmental level on both sides without endobronchial lesions. Transbronchial biopsies obtained under fluoroscopy. Minimal bleeding, settled with wedge. Post-procedure fluoroscopy without pneumothorax.
Complications: none.
Disposition: discharged home with escort.
Pathology addendum 02/21: yeast forms within macrophages consistent with histoplasmosis; no malignancy.
Allergies: NKDA.

medications.sig: Take 2 capsules (200 mg) by mouth three times daily with food for 3 days, then 2 capsules twice daily

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Re: David Thayer, DOB 12/02/1979. Telephone visit 02/24/2025.

Pathology from the 02/19 transbronchial biopsies shows small ovoid yeast within macrophages, consistent with histoplasmosis, and no malignancy. With three months of symptoms, weight loss and diffuse nodules, we are treating this as subacute pulmonary histoplasmosis.

Started itraconazole: 200 mg three times daily for the first 3 days, then 200 mg twice daily, planned for 12 weeks. Take with food. He was told about nausea, rash and rare liver injury.
Itraconazole can raise glipizide levels; please watch for hypoglycemia and consider a liver panel at about 4 weeks. We will see him in about 12 weeks with a repeat chest film.

Allergies: NKDA. Current medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg daily, itraconazole as above.

Pulmonology

documents.title: Your new medicine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: David, I got the lung doctor's letter. Glad it isn't cancer and that there's a clear treatment. The itraconazole can make glipizide stronger, so your sugar could run low. Eat breakfast before you take glipizide, keep juice or glucose tabs in the truck, and check your sugar if you feel shaky or sweaty. If you get a reading under 70, message me and we'll cut the glipizide. Let's see you in about a month and check your liver tests then.

documents.title: Re: Your new medicine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thanks. picked it up yesterday, big bottle. will keep candy in the truck

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four weeks into itraconazole. Cough is clearly less, only a few spells a day. No sweats in two weeks. Energy coming back, worked full days last week. Some mild nausea the first days, gone. No rash, no dark urine, no yellowing.
Sugars: fasting 160s, no readings under 80, no shaky spells.
Still smoking, 'maybe a little less.'

Exam: looks better than in January. Weight up a little. Afebrile. Lungs with a few crackles at both bases, fewer than before. Heart regular. No jaundice.

Plan: liver panel today per pulmonology. Continue itraconazole to finish 12 weeks; pulm visit in May. Diabetes meds unchanged. Physical in June.

documents.title: Liver panel
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver panel normal on itraconazole. Copy faxed to pulmonology. Portal note to pt.

reports.text:
Clinical history: pulmonary histoplasmosis on treatment.
Technique: PA and lateral views.
Comparison: 01/28/2025.
Findings: The small nodular opacities in both lungs are fewer and smaller than before. The hila are smaller, with less lymphadenopathy. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Interval improvement of bilateral nodular opacities and hilar lymphadenopathy.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE FOLLOW-UP (outside group)
Date of service: 05/20/2025
Re: David Thayer

Mr. Thayer has finished 12 weeks of itraconazole for subacute pulmonary histoplasmosis. Cough, fevers and night sweats have resolved. He has regained some weight and his energy is back to normal. He tolerated the drug; a liver panel at 4 weeks was normal.

Exam: well appearing. Lungs clear today. Heart regular.
Chest radiograph today: nodular opacities fewer and smaller, hilar nodes smaller.

Assessment: pulmonary histoplasmosis, treated, with clinical and radiographic response. Itraconazole stopped today.
Plan: no further routine pulmonary follow-up is needed; we are glad to see him again for any new respiratory symptoms. We again urged him to stop smoking and to use a fitted respirator for attic and crawl-space work.

Medications now: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Pulmonology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M, yearly exam. Finished the antifungal last month, pulmonology has signed off. Feels back to himself, no cough. Busy season at work.
Diabetes: takes metformin twice a day 'unless I forget the night one' and glipizide in the morning. Fasting 170s. No lows since stopping itraconazole.
Tobacco: pack a day. Says he knows. Not ready.
Mood fine, sleeping ok.

Exam: vitals as charted. Ears and throat clear. Lungs clear throughout. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft. Feet: no ulcers or calluses, monofilament intact, pulses palpable. Skin fine.

A/P:
1. T2DM. A1c 9.0 today. Went over diet and the missed evening doses again; he'll set a phone alarm. Same regimen for now. Lipids and urine albumin today. Eye exam due November.
2. Tobacco: advised to quit, declines meds.
3. Histoplasmosis, treated. Nothing further.
4. Prevention: turning 45 meant colon screening is due; he prefers the stool test, will hand him a FIT kit at his fall vaccine visit.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Same-day Visit - Leg
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning about his leg, came in at 11.

S: Three days of pain and redness in the left lower leg, spreading. Felt hot and had chills at home over the weekend, thermometer read low 100s. Can't recall hitting it or any bug bite, though he's in and out of debris all day. No prior leg infections. Diabetes as before, missed a few days of meds last week on a job out of town.

O: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), HR 88, BP 135/85. Looks uncomfortable but not toxic. Left leg: red, warm and tender from just above the ankle to the mid-calf, edges indistinct. No drainage, no fluctuant area, no blistering. Not much swelling, calves symmetric. No streaking. Between the toes clean. Right leg normal. Lungs clear.

Labs drawn here: WBC 12.0, Hgb 14, Plt 250, CRP 24. A1c 9.3. Blood cultures sent since he's febrile.

A/P:
1. Nonpurulent cellulitis, left lower leg. Stable vitals, eating and drinking, reliable. Outpatient: cephalexin 500 mg four times a day for 7 days. Skin-marker outline of the red border done. Elevate when he can, take a couple of days off ladders. Go to the ED for redness racing past the line, high fever, vomiting or feeling faint.
2. T2DM, A1c 9.3. Infection won't help sugars this week. Back on schedule with both meds.

RN to call Wednesday with cultures. Recheck Monday.

documents.title: RN Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt. Blood cultures no growth at 48 hrs, reviewed with PCP. Pt says redness is inside the marker line now, pain better, no fever since yesterday morning. Taking cephalexin 4x/day. Keep Monday appt.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up - Leg
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Leg much better. Afebrile since Wednesday. One day left of cephalexin. Back at work.
Exam: afebrile. Left calf with faint pink discoloration well inside the old marker line, no warmth, nontender. No swelling.
A/P: cellulitis resolving well, finish the course. Keep skin on the legs covered on job sites. Diabetes visit in the fall, flu shot then.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Seen 02/03/2026
Patient: David Thayer, 46M, DOB 12/02/1979

CC: short of breath, cough, fever.

HPI: Two days of worsening breathlessness with a cough bringing up yellow sputum, plus fevers. Known poorly controlled type 2 diabetes; prior histoplasmosis treated last year. No travel. No sick contacts he knows of.
PMH: type 2 diabetes; histoplasmosis (treated 2025); cellulitis left leg (2025); tobacco use disorder. PSH: tonsillectomy.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 10 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: smoker, 30 pack-years. Social alcohol.

Triage: T 38.7 C (101.7 F), HR 110, RR 28, SpO2 92% on room air.
Exam: ill appearing, tachypneic, speaking in full sentences. Crackles over the right lower lobe; left side clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. No leg swelling.

Results: WBC 18.0, Hgb 14, Plt 250. BUN 28, Cr 1.2, glucose 300; bicarbonate and anion gap normal, so DKA is not present. CXR: right lower lobe consolidation.

MDM: community-acquired pneumonia with hypoxemia and tachypnea in a poorly controlled diabetic, plus hyperglycemia without ketoacidosis and a BUN/Cr suggesting dehydration. IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin given, IV fluids, insulin started.

Disposition: admitted to medicine.

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days
Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 4 days

documents.title: Discharge Against Medical Advice
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - INPATIENT MEDICINE
Admitted 02/03/2026. Left against medical advice 02/04/2026.

Diagnosis: community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe. Uncontrolled type 2 diabetes with hyperglycemia; diabetic ketoacidosis excluded.

Course: admitted from the ED on IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin, IV fluids and subcutaneous insulin. After about 24 hours of treatment he asked to go home, worried about what the hospital stay would cost him. The team explained that leaving before treatment was complete risked the infection worsening and respiratory failure. He understood and still chose to leave. He signed the against-medical-advice form.

At departure he was given prescriptions for amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 7 days and azithromycin 250 mg daily for 4 days, and told to resume metformin and glipizide. Return precautions given. Advised follow-up with his primary care physician within a week.

Allergies: NKDA.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: RN Call - left hospital AMA
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hospital notified us pt left AMA yesterday with pneumonia. Called him. Says he feels 'wiped out but better than Tuesday.' Took both antibiotics last night and this morning. Fever 99.8 this morning. Breathing ok at rest, winded on stairs. Sugars 250s. Encouraged hydration. Reviewed reasons to go back in: harder breathing, lips blue, confusion, fever not breaking. Appt with PCP Tues 2/10, earlier if worse. He apologized about the cost thing, told him no apology needed, we'd rather hear from him.

events.reason: Follow-up after pneumonia, left hospital AMA

medications.drug: 3 ML insulin glargine 100 UNT/ML Pen Injector

orders.reason: confirm clearing of right lower lobe pneumonia

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED visit and one-night admission for right lower lobe pneumonia 2/3, left AMA 2/4 over cost. Hospital records reviewed: WBC 18.0, BUN 28, Cr 1.2, glucose 300, no DKA, RLL consolidation on film; discharged on amox-clav x7 days and azithro x4 days.

Today: on day 6 of amox-clav, azithro done. Fever gone since Friday. Cough still productive but looser, sputum lighter. Breathing near normal at rest, a little short on stairs. Eating and drinking. Fasting sugars 220-260 all week.
We talked about the cost worry. He has BCBS, the deductible scared him. Told him to call or text me first next time and we'll sort out the safest place to go. Front desk gave him the hospital's financial assistance number.

Exam: afebrile, SpO2 96% RA, RR normal. Looks tired but well. A few crackles at the right base, otherwise clear. Heart regular. No edema.
BMP today: Cr 0.9, BUN normal, so the hospital numbers were dehydration. A1c 10.2.

A/P:
1. CAP, RLL, improving on oral therapy. Finish amox-clav. Repeat chest x-ray in about 6 weeks given 30 pack-years.
2. T2DM, A1c 10.2 on metformin 1000 BID and glipizide 10. This needs more. Starting insulin glargine 10 units at bedtime, pen taught by RN today with a saline practice shot. Raise by 2 units every 3 days until fasting sugar is 90-130; stop increasing and call for any reading under 80. Continue metformin and glipizide. Send me numbers in 2 weeks.
3. BUN and creatinine back to normal.
4. Tobacco: he smoked through the pneumonia. Offered patch or varenicline again; still no.

RTC 2 months with A1c.

documents.title: Insulin Teaching
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Insulin pen teaching done: priming, dialing dose, abdomen site rotation, needle disposal in a hard container, storage of open pen. Pt demonstrated with practice pen. Low sugar rule of 15 reviewed. Log sheet given.

documents.body: up to 16 units now. mornings 158, 171, 149, 162, 144. no lows. cough just a little in am.

documents.title: Re: sugars
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nice work, that's real progress. Keep going up 2 units every 3 days until mornings are under 130. Same rule if you ever see under 80: stop going up and let me know. X-ray in late March.

reports.text:
Indication: follow-up of right lower lobe pneumonia, February 2026.
Technique: PA and lateral views.
Comparison: 05/20/2025 outside film.
Findings: The right lower lobe is clear; no residual consolidation. Lungs clear bilaterally. Hilar contours normal. No effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Resolution of right lower lobe pneumonia. No acute cardiopulmonary process.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Glargine since February. Titrated himself up and has sat at 18 units for about three weeks; mornings mostly 130s-140s, nothing under 90. Hasn't missed a night, keeps the pen by the coffee maker. Still on metformin and glipizide. Cough gone. CXR in March was clear.
Smoking: still about a pack a day.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Injection sites fine, no lumps. Feet normal, monofilament intact.
A1c 8.4, down from 10.2.

A/P:
1. T2DM, much better. Glargine 18 units nightly as the standing dose; new script written at that dose so the pharmacy count matches. He may nudge up 2 units if fasting stays above 130 for a week. Continue metformin 1000 BID, glipizide 10 daily.
2. Tobacco: asked again about a quit date; he will think about it.

Physical in July.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M, yearly visit plus diabetes check. Good stretch since the spring: no infections, no cough, working full days. Glargine 18 units nightly, metformin 1000 twice a day, glipizide 10 in the morning. Fasting sugars 120s-140s. One reading of 84 after a long day on a roof without lunch, felt fine.
Still about a pack a day. Says the pneumonia rattled him more than the fungus did. Still no quit date. Alcohol unchanged.
Mood good. PHQ-2 1.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft. Skin: legs without redness or breaks. Feet: no ulcers, sensation intact, pulses 2+.

A/P:
1. T2DM, improving. A1c today 7.8. Same regimen. Talked about not skipping meals on glipizide days. Lipids, kidney, urine albumin today. Eye exam due November.
2. Tobacco dependence. Advised to quit; offered varenicline or patches with a quit date of his choosing. Declines for now.
3. Prevention: FIT due in October, kit at the fall vaccine visit. Flu and COVID in the fall.

RTC October for diabetes.
